narr: A closed upper low pressure system exited the Desert Southwest into the Southern Rockies/New Mexico during the morning of May 17th, with a shortwave trough rotating northeast ahead of the low across Central and Southeast Texas. A very moist air mass was already in place across Deep East Texas ahead of this disturbance, with periods of showers and thunderstorms containing locally heavy rainfall developing over Southeast Texas and spreading northeast into Southern San Augustine and Sabine Counties from the early morning through midday of the 17th. Rainfall amounts of 3-6 inches were recorded across these areas, atop already saturated grounds from widespread heavy rainfall that fell about a week prior on May 9th. The heavy rainfall quickly ran off, resulting in flash flooding of a couple of major highways in Southern Sabine County.
ev: Highway 87 South in the Yellowpine community and Highway 96 in Brookeland were covered in high water.
lsr: SOME ROADS AND AREAS IN SABINE COUNTY ARE EXPERIENCING FLOODING: HIGHWAY 87 S YELLOWPINE AREA 96 IN BROOKELAND HIGHWAY 21 TO NACOGDOCHES ANGELINA RIVER.
